subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Corrosion: The Silent Destroyer
description: A quick, practical guide to Corrosion: The Silent Destroyer.

hook.text: Corrosion costs the global economy $2.5 trillion per year — more than natural disasters combined.

buildup.text: Iron reacts with oxygen and water to form rust. Rust occupies 6 times the volume of the original iron, cracking concrete.

discovery.text: Galvanic corrosion happens when two different metals touch in moisture. One sacrifices itself to protect the other.

twist.text: Ships bolt zinc plates to their hulls as sacrificial anodes. The zinc corrodes first, saving the steel hull.

climax.text: The Morandi Bridge in Genoa collapsed in 2018 partly due to corroded cables hidden inside concrete. 43 people died.

punchline.text: Invisible. Slow. Inevitable. Corrosion never stops.

quiz.question: How do sacrificial anodes protect ship hulls from corrosion?
options: They create a waterproof barrier between the hull and seawater
Zinc corrodes first in galvanic corrosion, saving the steel hull
They release chemicals that neutralize salt in the surrounding water
